A copy of the graph, its attributes and its stored memberships.
Canonical per-vertex community memberships.
doc.description:
One (non-empty) list of integer community labels per vertex: the
last result of :meth:`community_hedonic`, or what was assigned.
``None`` means no state. The setter accepts the flat partition form
(and tuples or NumPy arrays) and stores the normalized
list-of-lists. A call starts from this state only when it is passed
as ``initial_membership``. Assign a new state rather than editing the
returned lists in place (an edit is not validated), and note that
editing the graph does not update it.

members.name: validate_membership
members.signature: validate_membership(membership: list[int] | list[list[int]], *, overlapping: bool = False, max_memberships: int | None = None) -> bool

doc.summary: Whether ``membership`` is a valid membership state of this graph.
doc.description:
Disjoint (``overlapping=False``):
  - length == n (flat labels, or nested singleton rows)
  - non-negative integer labels
  - labels contiguous from 0

Overlapping (``overlapping=True``):
  - length == n
  - each entry is a non-empty list of non-negative community ids
    (one membership list per vertex), **or** a flat disjoint vector
    (accepted and later expanded to singleton lists). Duplicate labels
    in one row are rejected.

With ``max_memberships``, no row may hold more labels. This checks a
state strictly. ``community_hedonic`` is more lenient with a start:
it reads a repeated label in a row once, renumbers labels with gaps
in their order, and projects a row with more than
``max_memberships`` labels to the ones its vertex prefers.

members.name: community_hedonic
members.signature: community_hedonic(initial_membership: list[int] | list[list[int]] | None = None, *positional, max_communities: int | None = None, max_memberships: int = 1, resolution: float | None = None, allow_isolation: bool = False, edge_weights=None, seed: int | None = None, node_weights=None, max_total_communities: int | None = None, n_communities: int | None = None, **removed)

parameters.name: initial_membership
parameters.description:
The start. ``None`` (the default) is the singleton start, a
random start with ``max_communities``, or a feasible round-robin
start when a community-count limit is set. Otherwise one entry
per vertex: a community label (a partition) or a list of labels
(a cover); labels are non-negative integers, and labels with
gaps are renumbered in their order (0, 2, 5 become 0, 1, 2). A
list, tuple or NumPy array is accepted, as is an igraph
``VertexClustering`` or ``VertexCover`` of a graph with the same
vertices. A label repeated in a row counts once. To continue from
the previous result, pass ``initial_membership=g.memberships``.
A vertex with more labels than ``max_memberships`` keeps the
``max_memberships`` it prefers, ranked by the payoff of belonging
to each community alone, evaluated on the start as given (ties
to the larger community, then the smaller label); the detector
then moves from there to an equilibrium. A cover passed to a
partition call (``max_memberships=1``) thus becomes the partition
in which every vertex keeps its preferred community.
``_hedonic_provenance["projected_vertices"]`` counts the vertices
that had to choose.

parameters.name: max_communities
parameters.description:
Initialization only: when ``initial_membership`` is ``None`` and
``max_memberships == 1``, random start over ``[0, max_communities)``
(labels a draw leaves unused are dropped and the rest renumbered
in order).
It has no effect with a supplied start, with overlapping defaults,
or when community-count limits select a feasible default start;
``_hedonic_provenance["max_communities_effect"]`` records which
case applied. It is not an output constraint (see
``max_total_communities``/``n_communities``), but without
``allow_isolation`` no vertex can open a new community, so the
result then has at most ``max_communities`` communities.

parameters.name: max_memberships
parameters.description:
Per-vertex cap. ``1`` (default) gives a partition
(``VertexClustering``); ``> 1`` gives an overlapping cover
(``VertexCover``) in which each vertex belongs to at most this
many communities. ``-1`` removes the practical per-vertex cap (the
effective cap is the vertex count, recorded in
``_hedonic_provenance``).

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description:
CPM resolution γ. Defaults to the weighted density, the total
edge weight ``W`` over the number of vertex pairs (the density of
a simple unweighted graph). Must be a finite real. Smaller values
give larger communities. A total edge weight ``W <= 0`` is
rejected: the quality, the potential divided by ``W``, is
undefined.

parameters.name: allow_isolation
parameters.description: Allow a vertex to open a new, empty community.

parameters.name: edge_weights
parameters.description:
Optional edge weights (a sequence of real numbers in edge order,
or an edge-attribute name), finite; non-negative for covers. A
partition accepts negative weights as long as ``W > 0``. An edge
attribute named ``"weight"`` is not used unless named here.
Booleans, strings, complex numbers, ``None`` and dicts are
refused. The sum of their absolute values must stay below about
4e304, and ``W`` must be a normal double (at least about 2.2e-308).

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description:
When given, the visiting order is drawn from
``random.Random(seed)``, and the same seed drives the random
disjoint start. The returned labels are then a function of the
graph, weights, parameters, start state and seed. ``None`` draws
from Python's ``random`` module (python-igraph's default
generator), so ``random.seed(...)`` also makes a run repeatable.
Any integer is a seed, negative ones included, as for
``random.Random``. The visiting order follows the vertex ids and
each vertex's edges in the graph's edge order, so a repeatable run
also needs the same vertex numbering and edge order.

parameters.name: node_weights
parameters.description:
Optional vertex weights ``w_v`` (a sequence of real numbers in
vertex order, or a vertex-attribute name), finite and
non-negative. They enter the crowding term ``γ w_u w_v``; unit
weights are the default. ``|resolution| x N² x max_memberships``,
for the total vertex weight ``N``, must stay below about 4e304.

parameters.name: max_total_communities
parameters.description:
Optional upper bound on the number of occupied communities of the
result and of every state visited.

parameters.name: n_communities
parameters.description:
Optional exact number of occupied communities. Without a start
state, a deterministic round-robin start occupies all ``K``
labels. A start state that violates either count limit (after
its projection to ``max_memberships``) is rejected.

doc.summary: Community detection with the CPM hedonic game, disjoint or overlapping.
doc.description:
Each vertex is an agent that moves to the community (or, for covers,
the set of at most ``max_memberships`` communities) it prefers, one
vertex at a time, until no vertex can improve: every vertex is
visited, in a random order, and revisited after a neighbour moves.
A move is taken only when its computed gain exceeds a rigorous bound
of its rounding error, so every move raises the exact potential and
every call terminates. At return no unilateral deviation raises a
vertex's exact payoff by more than
``_hedonic_provenance["equilibrium_slack"]`` times the total edge
weight. For a partition the slack is 0 whenever no deviation's exact
gain can be positive: always when the arithmetic is exact (for
instance unit weights at resolution 0, 1/2 or 1), and often
otherwise; the result is then an exact Nash equilibrium. Covers,
whose payoffs divide by square roots, keep a tiny positive slack
(about 1e-15 on small graphs, less on large ones). The result
is an equilibrium reached from the start, not the best partition or
cover: from singletons at resolution 0, for instance, a connected
graph need not end as one community. The computation runs in this
package's C core (``hedonic._core``). Every argument after
``initial_membership`` is keyword-only.

The graph must be undirected and free of self-loops (a loop ties a
vertex to no one else; ``g.simplify(multiple=False, loops=True)``
removes them). Parallel edges count as one edge whose weight is
their sum.

VertexClustering if ``max_memberships == 1``, else VertexCover.

The result carries ``_hedonic_provenance`` (versions, effective
parameters, count mode) and ``_hedonic_native_quality``:
``(Φ - γ Σ_v n_v² / 2) / W`` for the exact potential ``Φ`` of the
returned state (a sum over pairs of vertices), the vertex weights
``n_v`` (1 by default) and the total edge weight ``W``; the constant
term is each vertex's own crowding, the same for every state. The returned
memberships are also stored in ``self.memberships``; pass
``initial_membership=g.memberships`` to continue from them.

Every vertex of a cover keeps at least one community: the actions are
the non-empty sets of at most ``max_memberships`` labels (with
``allow_isolation`` one of them is a new community of its own, worth
0). A cover can return two labels with the same members; they are
kept apart, as the equilibrium is a statement about labels.

The binding holds the GIL for the whole call, so calls from several
threads are safe but run one at a time (use processes to run them in
parallel); with ``seed=None`` they also share the ``random`` module's
state.

non-negative. They enter the crowding term ``γ w_u w_v``; unit
weights are the default. ``|resolution| x N² x max_memberships``,
for the total vertex weight ``N``, must stay below about 4e304.

Optional upper bound on the number of occupied communities of the
result and of every state visited.

Optional exact number of occupied communities. Without a start
state, a deterministic round-robin start occupies all ``K``
labels. A start state that violates either count limit (after
its projection to ``max_memberships``) is rejected.

functions.name: sample_uniform_ints
functions.signature: sample_uniform_ints(N: int, K: int, seed: int)

doc.summary: Sample N uniform integers from [0, K] using a seeded NumPy RNG.
doc.description: Uses NumPy's Generator (PCG64) for reproducible, vectorized sampling.

doc.summary: The detector's quality (potential) stored on a VertexClustering or VertexCover.

Group a flat label vector (one hashable label per vertex) into
communities, ordered by label when the labels sort, else by first
appearance.

Convert a VertexClustering, VertexCover or flat membership vector to
community lists.
Disjoint membership vector → overlapping initial_membership format.
``cover`` restricted to the vertices that ``reference`` covers.
doc.description:
Every community keeps only its vertices that belong to some community of
``reference``, in their order; a community left empty is dropped. This is
how a prediction on a whole graph is scored against a reference that
labels only part of it.

doc.summary: Convert community lists to the canonical per-vertex Game state.
doc.description:
Vertices absent from a predicted cover receive deterministic singleton
labels.  This is the same representation persisted by
:meth:`hedonic.Game.community_hedonic`, making the helper convenient for
notebooks and experiment adapters that already have a cover in list form.

functions.name: score_cover
functions.signature: score_cover(graph: Any, ground_truth: Sequence[Sequence[int]], cover: Sequence[Sequence[int]], *, metrics: Sequence[str] = GAME_EVALUATION_METRICS, omega_sample_size: int = 100000, seed: int = 0, restrict_to_reference: bool = False) -> dict[str, float | None]

doc.summary: Score a cover through the public :class:`hedonic.Game` facade.
doc.description:
The defaults are those of :meth:`hedonic.Game.evaluate_against`. Vertices
the cover leaves out play alone (``cover_to_memberships``), so they count
as singleton predictions; pass ``restrict_to_reference=True`` to score
only the vertices the reference covers. The import is local so the
metrics package remains usable without making the core package eagerly
import the optional experiment machinery.

functions.name: one_to_one_community_metrics
functions.signature: one_to_one_community_metrics(predicted: Sequence[Sequence[int]], ground_truth: Sequence[Sequence[int]], *, matching_weight: MatchingWeight = 'f1', singleton_mode: SingletonMode = 'all') -> dict[str, float | int | str]

doc.summary: One-to-one community precision/recall/F1 with zero unmatched scores.
doc.description:
Matched-pair precision is averaged over *all predicted* communities and
matched-pair recall over *all GT* communities.  Thus an unmatched predicted
community contributes zero precision and an unmatched GT community
contributes zero recall.  ``matching_f1`` is their harmonic mean.

When several assignments reach the maximum total weight, the solver picks
one; covers above ``MAX_DENSE_MATCHING_CELLS`` pair cells are matched by
a sparse solver that can pick another, so these scores can differ between
the two paths on tied inputs (the total weight does not).

functions.name: node_membership_multilabel_metrics
functions.signature: node_membership_multilabel_metrics(predicted: Sequence[Sequence[int]], ground_truth: Sequence[Sequence[int]], *, matching_weight: MatchingWeight = 'f1', singleton_mode: SingletonMode = 'all') -> dict[str, float]

doc.summary: Multilabel membership scores after one-to-one community alignment.
doc.description:
Micro scores count vertex-community assignments.  Macro F1 is the standard
label-wise multilabel macro average over the label space after alignment:
every GT label (a matched predicted community takes its GT label) plus the
unmatched predicted labels, that is ``|predicted| + |GT| - |matches|``
labels; an unmatched label, on either side, receives F1 zero.

functions.signature: symmetric_best_match_f1(predicted: Sequence[Sequence[int]], ground_truth: Sequence[Sequence[int]], *, singleton_mode: SingletonMode = 'all') -> float

doc.summary: Historical macro best-match F1, averaged in both directions.

functions.name: overlapping_normalized_mutual_information_lfk
functions.signature: overlapping_normalized_mutual_information_lfk(predicted: Sequence[Sequence[int]], ground_truth: Sequence[Sequence[int]], *, n_vertices: int | None = None) -> float

doc.summary: Compute the LFK overlapping normalized mutual information (ONMI).
doc.description:
The CoDeSEG paper delegates ONMI to the LFK/OvpNMI implementation.  This
experiment-layer implementation keeps the same pairwise entropy definition
but enumerates only positive community intersections, so it remains usable
on the full SNAP covers.  ``n_vertices`` controls the universe used for
entropy; omit it to reproduce the paper's evaluation convention of using
the union of vertices appearing in either cover.

doc.summary: Historical best-match metrics without computing Hungarian alignment.

functions.name: cover_diagnostics
functions.signature: cover_diagnostics(predicted: Sequence[Sequence[int]], ground_truth: Sequence[Sequence[int]], n_vertices: int, *, singleton_mode: SingletonMode = 'all') -> dict[str, float | int | None]

functions.name: structural_overlap_metrics
functions.signature: structural_overlap_metrics(predicted: Sequence[Sequence[int]], ground_truth: Sequence[Sequence[int]], *, singleton_mode: SingletonMode = 'all', max_pair_events: int = 100000) -> dict[str, float | int | bool]

doc.summary: Bounded structural overlap metrics, separate from recovery accuracy.
doc.description:
``inclusion_rate`` is the mean fraction of each predicted community covered
by its best ground-truth match.  ``coverage_rate`` is its inverse
ground-truth direction.  ``overlapping_rate`` is the mean normalized
intersection (intersection / smaller community) across predicted community
pairs that share a node.  ``distribution_rate`` is the fraction of
predicted memberships assigned to nodes with multiple memberships.

Pair intersections are accumulated from an inverted index and stop after
``max_pair_events`` events; this deliberately avoids dense community-pair
matrices on the largest SNAP covers.  The truncation flag must accompany
comparisons where this bound is reached.

functions.name: evaluate_cover
functions.signature: evaluate_cover(predicted: Sequence[Sequence[int]], ground_truth: Sequence[Sequence[int]], n_vertices: int, compute_omega: bool = True, *, singleton_mode: SingletonMode = 'all', matching_weight: MatchingWeight = 'f1', omega_sample_size: int = 100000, omega_seed: int = 0, one_to_one: bool = True) -> dict

doc.summary: Evaluate a cover with legacy and recommended overlap-aware metrics.
doc.description:
Vertices are integers in ``range(n_vertices)``. ``one_to_one=False``
skips the one-to-one matching (and the metrics built on it, which are
then absent), the only part that needs SciPy.

Both covers are read as sets of vertex sets (``SCORE_DEFINITION``):
repeated members count once and communities with the same members are
collapsed into one before scoring (``n_pred_comms`` and ``n_gt_comms``
count them after the collapse); ``singleton_mode="size_ge_2"`` then drops
communities of one vertex. A vertex absent from a cover is in none of its
communities. When a side is empty, a precision or recall over it is 0, so
the community and vertex F1 and Jaccard scores are 0; for two empty
covers, Omega, ``node_macro_f1`` and ``matching_mean_weight`` are 1 (as
is ONMI, :func:`overlapping_normalized_mutual_information_lfk`). Omega is a sampled estimate
(``omega_sample_size`` vertex pairs drawn with ``omega_seed``); ``nf1``
follows its reference implementation (see :func:`normalized_f1_rossetti`).

doc.summary: NF1 of Rossetti, Pappalardo & Rinzivillo (2016), as used by ANGEL.
doc.description:
A faithful port of the reference implementation (``NF1`` in CDlib 0.4.0,
``cdlib/evaluation/internal/NF1.py``), including its conventions: each
detected community is matched to the reference communities with the largest
member count among its vertices (ties give several matches); a vertex is
counted only in the first detected community in which it appears; each
match's F1 is rounded to two decimals. NF1 = mean F1 x coverage / redundancy,
where coverage is the fraction of reference communities matched and
redundancy is the number of detected communities per matched reference
community.

As in the reference, the covers are used as given: duplicate communities
are not collapsed and ``singleton_mode`` does not apply, and NF1 exceeds 1
when there are fewer detected communities than matched reference ones (one
detected community tied between two reference communities, for instance).

functions.name: omega_index
functions.signature: omega_index(pred: Sequence[Sequence[int]], gt: Sequence[Sequence[int]], n: int, *, sample_size: int = 100000, seed: int = 0) -> float

doc.summary: Omega index, exact on small graphs and sampled on large ones.
doc.description:
When the graph has at most ``sample_size`` unordered vertex pairs, every
pair is counted once and the result is the exact Omega index (``seed`` is
then unused). Otherwise ``sample_size`` pairs are drawn uniformly with
replacement. Memory is O(total memberships + n + sample_size), with no
dense ``n × n`` allocation, making the metric safe for full DBLP. Use a
fixed ``seed`` for reproducible rescoring.

doc.summary: Fraction of vertices stable at each resolution (closed endpoints).
doc.description:
``intervals`` is the list returned by ``Game.stable_intervals`` and
``resolutions`` is a one-dimensional grid in [0, 1]. An empty population
has stable fraction NaN. Overlapping intervals count their owner once.

doc.summary: Mean stable shares of linear and logarithmic resolution, as a pair.
doc.description:
Linear measure averages the lengths in [0, 1]. Log measure averages the
lengths in log10 resolution on [log10(log_floor), 0]; the default floor
is 1e-4 (four decades). An empty population returns (NaN, NaN).

doc.summary: Intersect every vertex's closed stable set, in vertex order.
doc.description:
Returns a list of (lo, hi) pairs. An empty population imposes no
constraints and returns [(0, 1)]; any never-stable vertex returns [].
